title: The Great Return as conditional arrival
statement: The canon anticipates an official arrival of the Elohim on Earth — the culminating event its message is oriented toward — and makes it conditional rather than predicted: humanity must want the return, must be sufficiently unified and wise to receive advanced knowledge responsibly, must build the Embassy on extraterritorial ground, and must guarantee the visitors' safety; the anticipation is situated in the contemporary period the canon calls the Apocalypse, coextensive with the Age of Aquarius and opening at the mid-twentieth-century threshold, and the arrival would inaugurate a transfer of knowledge far in advance of humanity's own.

includes: The conditionality, which is load-bearing: the return is contingent on human choices the canon enumerates, so the claim asserts an anticipated conditional event, never a dated prophecy
The period placement: the Apocalypse read as unveiling-period, coextensive with the Age of Aquarius, opening at the 1945/1946 threshold the canon sets and woh-claim-0003 anchors astronomically
The content of the anticipated event as the canon states it: official contact, meetings with humanity's representatives, and the knowledge transfer
The Embassy condition as a pointer to woh-claim-0016, which carries the structure itself
excludes: Any date for the arrival; the canon's conditionality forbids date-setting and so does this record
Any claim that current events confirm or disconfirm the anticipation; the record is about what the canon anticipates, not about news
Apocalypse as destruction; the record fixes the unveiling sense against the popular one
The probability of the event, which the corpus does not model

source_references.locator: 'The New Commandments — Your Mission' (the conditions and the embassy instruction); the closing orientation of the message toward the return
The second message's elaboration of the reception conditions and the period
The academic account of the movement's return-orientation and its sociology

alternatives.statement: The conditional return is standard millenarian structure — a deferred culmination whose conditions explain non-arrival — and the scholarly literature on new religious movements reads it as such.
The conditions function as a mobilization device for the movement (build, unify, want), independent of any anticipated event.
The Aquarius/Apocalypse placement retrofits an astrological convention onto a twentieth-century founding date.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0003 is revised or retired.
The canon's fuller context changes the enumerated conditions or the period placement.
Public prose begins date-setting or reading news events as confirmation, which this record excludes.
Claim woh-claim-0016 (the Embassy) is revised in a way that changes the condition structure.
